_schema.range_name: a short identifier for this range (free text, used only in logs/README context, not by any script)
_schema.note: free-text note shown nowhere automatically — operators use this field for standing reminders about the range as a whole (e.g. naming/safety conventions). Scripts don't read it.
_schema.hosts: a map of golden_vmid (string) -> host record. golden_vmid is the Proxmox VMID of the existing, protected golden image — never a working clone's own VMID.

host record fields.host: hostname, without the '-golden'/'-ctf' suffix — scripts/prompts build '<host>-golden' and '<host>-ctf' from this
host record fields.os: 'Linux' or 'Windows' — informational only; no script branches on this field today
host record fields.ipv4: the golden image's own address, for reference only — real scans/PoC/remediation always target the WORKING clone's address (passed separately via --target at runtime), never this field
host record fields.note: optional free-text per-host note (e.g. a safety/isolation confirmation like the one this project used for a simulated-RTU-named host) — not read by any script, for human operators only

_schema.REMEMBER: this file is committed to a public repo as a TEMPLATE only. Keep your real, filled-in range inventory in a separate, untracked file (e.g. hosts.local.json, or this same filename added to .gitignore in your own private deployment) and pass it explicitly via --config — never commit real VMIDs/addresses for a non-public range.

note: Golden images (VMID as listed below) are never scanned, modified, or exploited directly. Every assessment run clones <host>-golden to a working image named <host>-ctf before touching it, and that working VM is destroyed at the end of the run.

9002.note: example of the optional per-host note field — e.g. an operator confirmation that this host is simulated/isolated, if that ever matters for a real entry
